silhouette_iou.why: CHOSEN: measured after aligning the generated silhouette to the reference by centroid and area (scale free, shape not -- the presentation gate's own rule); a 10 % change of aspect alone costs ~0.09 of IoU on a compact shape, so 0.80 admits that and the segmentation's edge noise and refuses a redrawn outline

aspect_drift.why: CHOSEN: the presentation gate's own geometry tolerance is 10 %

structure_ncc.why: CHOSEN, weak by design: normalised correlation of blurred gradient magnitude inside the reference silhouette says whether the rows and posts sit where the reference put them; 0.30 is well above what two unrelated textures give (~0) and is reported beside the number

hue_spread_deg.why: CHOSEN: one dyed yarn is one hue; a second colour region would read as a second mode far outside this

Photograph it as a real object made of real yarn: natural fibre texture with a little fuzz, soft window daylight from one side, a plain neutral tabletop, an ordinary camera. No text, nothing else in frame. The second image is the outline mask of the piece and the third shows its surface orientation; use them only to keep the piece's outline, position and surface placement exactly as in the first image.

silhouette_iou.why: CHOSEN: measured after aligning the generated silhouette to the reference by centroid and area (scale free, shape not -- the presentation gate's own rule); a 10 % change of aspect alone costs ~0.09 of IoU on a compact shape, so 0.80 admits that and the segmentation's edge noise and refuses a redrawn outline

aspect_drift.why: CHOSEN: the presentation gate's own geometry tolerance is 10 %

structure_ncc.why: CHOSEN, weak by design: normalised correlation of blurred gradient magnitude inside the reference silhouette says whether the rows and posts sit where the reference put them; 0.30 is well above what two unrelated textures give (~0) and is reported beside the number

hue_spread_deg.why: CHOSEN: one dyed yarn is one hue; a second colour region would read as a second mode far outside this

correspondence.questionnaire: This is an image of a crocheted swatch. Answer as JSON with exactly these keys, and give null for any value the image does not let you determine: "rows": integer number of horizontal rows of stitches you can count; "stitches_per_row": integer number of stitches you can count across one full row; "stitch_height": "short" if each stitch is about as tall as it is wide or less, "tall" if each stitch stands clearly taller than it is wide on a visible post; "loose_ends": where any loose strand ends are visible ("bottom", "top", "sides", "none", or a short phrase); "colours": integer number of distinct yarn colours; "shape": one short phrase for the overall outline (e.g. "upright rectangle", "square", "irregular"); "notes": one sentence on anything structurally notable.

reference_reading.raw:
{
  "rows": 5,
  "stitches_per_row": 5,
  "stitch_height": "tall",
  "loose_ends": "top and sides",
  "colours": 1,
  "shape": "upright rectangle",
  "notes": "Open, airy pattern with tall posts and wide gaps; edges are uneven and the bottom curls."
}

the relaxed fabric passes every Product Truth lock before any load
the rigidity the drape uses is derived from this fabric by the committed procedure and is curvature-independent to 1 per cent

the loaded configuration has lower total energy than the certified one

measured.frame: certified stitch frame carried by each stitch's own rigid motion
measured.morphology_held_by: friction lock (rigid_stitches): the stitch's internal shape is an input here, not an outcome; linkage, floor and clearance are outcomes

the curve file is derived from the draped fabric's own strands; every ply vertex lies within the yarn radius of its centreline; the fabric is not touched by drawing it
